claims.text: Controlled pre-oxidation can produce an in situ, dense, alumina-rich oxide interlayer on boride-based components.
The alumina-rich interlayer will significantly improve resistance of boride-based components to molten-aluminum corrosion.
Typical unmodified boride-based component surfaces are susceptible to rapid attack by molten aluminum.
A brief treatment in an oxygen-containing atmosphere can induce a continuous and adherent oxide layer.
The oxide produced by pre-oxidizing the boride-based component will be alumina-rich.
Matching hot-dip aluminum-plating thermal profiles and atmospheric composition during treatment will help the oxide remain effective during molten-aluminum exposure.
A dense alumina-rich oxide layer will act as a diffusion barrier between molten aluminum and the boride substrate.
Pre-oxidation will minimize direct contact between molten aluminum and the boride substrate.
Minimizing direct molten-aluminum contact will reduce elemental dissolution and interfacial reactions that drive corrosion.
Pre-oxidized components will have a lower corrosion rate or mass loss than untreated components during molten-aluminum exposure.
Pre-oxidized components will have a longer service life than untreated components.
Untreated boride-based components undergo rapid molten-aluminum penetration and accelerated corrosion because they lack a protective barrier.
Nonuniformity, porosity, or spallation of the oxide during thermal cycling may compromise its protective effectiveness.
Treatment temperature, duration, and atmosphere are critical to obtaining effective protection.
The optimal treatment conditions and the long-term adhesion and stability of the oxide under cyclic plating conditions remain undetermined.
